ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A body with a mass of $100\mathrm{kg}$ rests on the floor of a vertically moving elevator. The graph shows how the pressure of the body on the floor varies with time. The elevator starts from rest and moves upwards. The acceleration due to gravity ${\bf g}$ is taken as $10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$.

1. Determine the vertical displacement of the elevator within the first 8 seconds.

It shows a stepwise force: F = 1.5×10^3 N from 0 to 2 s, F = 1.0×10^3 N from 2 to 6 s, and F = 0.5×10^3 N from 6 to 8 s. Reasoning: The body's mass is m = 100 kg and g = 10 m/s^2, so mg = 1000 N. Starting from rest, s1 = 0.5×5×2^2 = 10 m, and v at 2 s is 10 m/s. For 2–6 s: F = 1000 N, so a = 0. The elevator moves at constant v = 10 m/s for 4 s, so s2 = 10×4 = 40 m. For 6–8 s: F = 500 N, so a = (500 - 1000)/100 = -5 m/s^2. With initial velocity 10 m/s for this interval, s3 = 10×2 + 0.5×(-5)×2^2 = 20 - 10 = 10 m. Total displacement in the first 8 s is s = 10 + 40 + 10 = 60 m upward.

method.method_draft: Read the graph as a stepwise normal force: from 0 to 2 s, F = 1.5×10^3 N; from 2 to 6 s, F = 1.0×10^3 N; from 6 to 8 s, F = 0.5×10^3 N. From the text, take m = 100 kg, g = 10 m/s^2, and initial elevator velocity 0. Use upward positive and apply F - mg = ma, giving accelerations +5 m/s^2, 0, and -5 m/s^2 on the three intervals. Then use constant-acceleration kinematics interval by interval: displacement over 0–2 s, update velocity; displacement over 2–6 s at constant velocity; displacement over 6–8 s while decelerating. Sum the three displacements to get 60 m.

method.method_draft: Read the same step graph values from the image, then transform the normal-force graph into an acceleration-time graph using a(t) = F(t)/m - g.
